3. The defendant No. 1 (kha) a substituted heir of defendant No. 1 and defendant No. 2, an added defendant contested the suit by filing two separate written statements almost on the same grounds inter-alia that the plaintiff had no cause of action; that the suit was bad for defect of parties; that the suit was barred by limitation and also by the principles of estoppel, waiver and acquisence. The defendants denied that there was any bainapatra (deed of contract) executed by Sarat Chandra Sarkar in favour of the plaintiff for sale of the suit-land or that the plaintiff paid in advance to the defendant a sum of Tk. 2,000/- as earnest money out of the total consideration. The defendants stated that the real facts were that Sarat Chandra Sarkar did not at all enter into any contract for sale of his land with the plaintiff. The defendant No. 1 (kha) stated that Sarat Chandra defendant No. 1 sold out only 5 bighas of his land from the suit-joma to the plaintiff who got executed by said Sarat Kumar a blank stamp-paper to be made a borga Kabuliyat but the plaintiff fraudulently made the same a bainapatra (deed of contract) for sale of the suit-land. The defendant No. 2 stated that he purchased the suit-land from Sarat by registered kabala deed dated 4.7.69 and since then he was possessing the same He further stated that he was not sware of the alleged bainapatra (deed of contract). 

 12. Mr. Latifur Rahman, however challenged the aforesaid judgment and decree of the court of appeal below on merit contending inter-alia that the lower appellate court by mistaken assumption of facts of the case and through misreading and also non-consideration of the evidence on record, particularly the evidence with regard to the first payment of the earnest money for an amount of Tk. 500/- by the plaintiff to the defendant No.1, late Sarat Chandra Sarkar who of course admitted his signature on the said document i.e. the deed of contract (Ekrarnama) Ext. 1, but denied the contents incorporated therein and contended that his signature was obtained not for making the deed of contract for sale of the suit-land, but for making a borga-kabuliyat for cultivation of the suit-land under the plaintiff, arrived at erroneous conclusion. He further submitted that the trial court carefully examined the genuineness of the said deed of contract, Ext. 1 as per the issues framed in the suit and considered the evidence on record as to the execution and the contents of the said document and rightly found the same to be fully genuine and decreed the suit which ought to have been upheld by the court of appeal below. 

 13. I have already stated above that the plaintiff in order to prove his case examined 5 P. Ws. and the contesting defendants examined 4 D. Ws. in support of their respective cases. P. W. 1 is the plaintiff himself. It is in his evidence that he earlier paid Taka 500/- to the defendant No. 1 Sarat Chandra Sarkar a few days before the execution of the deed of contract, Ext. l and thereafter at the time of actual execution of the same on the 28th Bhadra, 1370 B. S. he paid the rest amount of Tk. 1,500/- to the said executant defendant No.1 Sarat Chandra Sarkar, since deceased and he further stated that the total consideration was fixed at Tk. 2,500/- out of which he already paid up a sum of Tk. 2,000/- by two instalments as stated above and if the executant defendant No.1 Sarat Chandra Sarkar could return that money by Ashwin, 1375 B. S. and then he (Plaintiff) would have returned the deed of contract and also given up possession of the suit-land to him the defendant No.1 according to terms of contract but he i. e. Sarat Chandra Sarkar, the defendant No. 1 failed to do so. Now, in his cross-examination P.W. 1 could not be shaken on the above points in any way by the defendants. The plaintiff however brought Abul Hossain Haradar P. W. 3, the writer of the said deed of contract and also as a witness who categorically stated that he was a deed- writer of Rampal and he wrote the aforesaid deed of contract Ext. 1 under the instructions of defendant No.1 Sarat Chandra Sarkar. He of course stated that the payment of Tk. 1,500/- to the defendant No.1 was done in his presence, but it was also in the evidence of P. W. 1 that earlier the plaintiff paid Tk. 500/- to the defendant No. 1 Sarat Chandra Sarkar before the subsequent payment to Tk. 1,500/-. About the earlier payment of Tk. 500/- to the defendant No. 1, P. W. 4 Sheikh Arman also stated in his deposition. Of course, the sum of Tk. 1,500/-was paid in his presence to the executant Sarat Chandra Sarkar before the execution of the said deed of contract Ext. 1. A suggestion from the said of the contesting defendant was given to the above P.Ws. to the effect that the said document of contract was anti dated and meant for borga kabuliyat only, was totally denied by both of them, P. W. 3 was an attesting witness of the said deed of contract. He came to prove the execution of the said deed Ext.1 in his presence. Against these witnesses it appears that no enmity or grudge was suggested by defendant No.1.
